provenance.method: AI-authored summaries grounded in the supplied EPUB; original companion exercises

title.en: In the Beginning, There Is the Designer

summary.en: Design starts with making decisions and trying games, rather than waiting for permission to call yourself a designer. Schell makes deep listening the foundation of the work and treats love of the craft as a reason to keep practicing.
summary.zh: 设计始于作出决定和动手尝试，而不是等待别人认可自己是设计师。Schell 将深入倾听视为工作的基础，并强调对这份工作的热爱能支撑持续练习。

takeaways.en: Listen to the audience, team, game, client, and yourself; each reveals a different kind of design problem.
takeaways.zh: 倾听受众、团队、游戏、客户以及自己；每个对象都会揭示不同类型的设计问题。

takeaways.en: A broad skill set helps, but noticing what an experience is actually doing is more useful than defending an initial idea.
takeaways.zh: 广泛的技能有帮助，但察觉体验实际产生的效果，比维护最初的点子更有价值。

exercise.en: After a short play session, write one observation from each of the five listening perspectives. Turn the least certain observation into a question for your next session.
exercise.zh: 完成一次短暂试玩后，从五种倾听视角各写下一条观察。将最不确定的一条转化为下一次试玩要回答的问题。

title.en: The Designer Creates an Experience

summary.en: A game is an artifact that makes an experience possible. The chapter develops introspection as a practical design tool, while warning that your own response is neither an objective measurement nor a substitute for other players’ responses.
summary.zh: 游戏是让体验得以发生的作品。本章将内省发展为实用的设计工具，同时提醒我们：自己的反应既不是客观测量，也不能替代其他玩家的反应。

takeaways.en: Name specific emotions and the events that produced them instead of stopping at “good” or “bad.”
takeaways.zh: 明确说出具体情感及其触发事件，不要停留在“好”或“不好”。

takeaways.en: Preserve the essential qualities of an experience; a faithful simulation of every real-world detail is not required.
takeaways.zh: 保留体验的核心特质；不必忠实模拟现实中的每个细节。

exercise.en: Describe a memorable experience in three feelings. For each feeling, propose one rule, one visual cue, and one sound that could evoke it, then test the cheapest combination.
exercise.zh: 用三种感受描述一段难忘体验。为每种感受提出一条规则、一个视觉提示和一种声音，再测试成本最低的组合。

title.en: The Experience Takes Place in a Venue

summary.en: Where play happens shapes what a game can ask of people. The chapter looks beyond changing hardware platforms to relatively enduring patterns of private, public, and shared play spaces.
summary.zh: 游玩发生的场所决定了游戏适合向人提出怎样的要求。本章越过不断变化的硬件平台，考察相对持久的私人、公共与共享游玩空间。

takeaways.en: Attention, social exposure, physical movement, and session length depend on the venue.
takeaways.zh: 注意力、公开程度、身体活动和单次时长都受场所影响。

takeaways.en: A platform can serve several venues; matching the device does not automatically mean matching the situation.
takeaways.zh: 一个平台可以服务于多种场所；适配设备并不自动等于适配情境。

exercise.en: Describe your game being played at a desk and while waiting in a public place. Identify one interaction and one pacing decision that would need to change.
exercise.zh: 分别描述在书桌前和公共场所等候时玩你的游戏的情境。找出一种需要改变的交互，以及一项需要调整的节奏安排。

title.en: The Experience Rises Out of a Game

summary.en: The chapter uses definitions of play, toys, fun, and games to expose design properties rather than police category boundaries. It connects voluntary participation, goals, rules, and internally meaningful outcomes to the activity of solving problems.
summary.zh: 本章借助对玩耍、玩具、乐趣和游戏的定义来揭示设计特性，而非裁定类别边界。它把自愿参与、目标、规则以及游戏内有意义的结果，与解决问题的活动联系起来。

takeaways.en: A toy may be enjoyable to manipulate even before it has a goal; a game adds a structure for pursuing outcomes.
takeaways.zh: 玩具即使没有目标也可能值得摆弄；游戏则为追求结果增加了结构。

takeaways.en: Curiosity, surprise, and value created inside the game explain why otherwise arbitrary tasks can matter to players.
takeaways.zh: 好奇、惊喜以及在游戏内部形成的价值，可以解释为什么看似随意的任务会令玩家在意。

exercise.en: Choose one repeated task in your game. Write the problem it poses, why a player would care, and how the rules make its outcome valuable.
exercise.zh: 选择游戏中一项反复进行的任务，写明它提出了什么问题、玩家为何会在意，以及规则如何让结果具有价值。

title.en: The Game Consists of Elements

summary.en: Mechanics, story, aesthetics, and technology form a mutually supporting system. The designer needs to understand their structure while also keeping the lived player experience in view.
summary.zh: 机制、故事、美感与技术构成相互支持的系统。设计师既要理解其结构，也要始终关注玩家实际经历的体验。

takeaways.en: Improving one element in isolation can weaken the whole if it conflicts with the others.
takeaways.zh: 如果与其他要素冲突，孤立地加强某个要素反而可能削弱整体。

takeaways.en: Holographic design means holding the underlying system and the resulting experience together in your thinking.
takeaways.zh: 全息设计要求在思考中同时把握底层系统及其产生的体验。

exercise.en: Make a four-column table for one feature: mechanics, story, aesthetics, technology. Add a final row describing the player feeling each column should support.
exercise.zh: 为一个功能制作四列表格：机制、故事、美感、技术。再加一行，说明各列应支持玩家产生什么感受。

title.en: The Elements Support a Theme

summary.en: A theme provides a common direction for design decisions. A resonant theme goes further by connecting that direction to something players care about deeply.
summary.zh: 主题为设计决策提供共同方向。能引发共鸣的主题更进一步，将这个方向与玩家深切在意的事物联系起来。

takeaways.en: Use the theme to decide what belongs in the game and which elements should reinforce one another.
takeaways.zh: 用主题判断哪些内容属于游戏，以及哪些要素应相互强化。

takeaways.en: A unifying theme is useful even when players cannot state it explicitly or the game does not aim for a profound message.
takeaways.zh: 即使玩家无法明确说出主题，或者游戏并不追求深刻寓意，统一的主题仍然有用。

exercise.en: State your theme in one sentence. Inspect five concrete design choices and rewrite the weakest one so that it supports the same experience.
exercise.zh: 用一句话陈述主题。检查五项具体设计选择，改写其中最薄弱的一项，使其支持同一种体验。

title.en: The Game Begins with an Idea

summary.en: Idea generation becomes more productive when the problem and its constraints are clear. The chapter encourages looking outside games, recording ideas, and allowing the mind time and material to make unexpected connections.
summary.zh: 当问题与约束足够清晰时，创意生成会更有效。本章鼓励从游戏之外寻找素材、记录想法，并给头脑足够的时间与材料建立意外的联系。

takeaways.en: A problem statement should identify the desired result and genuine constraints without smuggling in a premature solution.
takeaways.zh: 问题陈述应指出期望结果与真实约束，而不是暗中预设解决方案。

takeaways.en: Externalizing many rough ideas makes it easier to combine them and challenge assumptions.
takeaways.zh: 将大量粗略想法记录下来，更容易组合它们并质疑既有假设。

exercise.en: Write a design problem without naming a genre. Generate ten possible solutions using experiences outside gaming, then combine two that initially seem unrelated.
exercise.zh: 不指定游戏类型，写下一个设计问题。从游戏之外的体验中提出十种可能解法，再组合两个起初看似无关的想法。

title.en: The Game Improves through Iteration

summary.en: Iteration turns an idea into evidence and then into a better design. The chapter uses risk assessment and question-driven prototypes to increase the number of useful learning loops within a limited budget.
summary.zh: 迭代把想法转化为证据，再转化为更好的设计。本章通过风险评估和围绕问题建立的原型，在有限预算内增加有效的学习循环。

takeaways.en: A prototype should answer a specific question; visual polish and complete implementation are often unnecessary.
takeaways.zh: 原型应回答一个明确问题；精美外观与完整实现往往并非必要。

takeaways.en: Recheck the design against multiple filters after changes, because solving one problem can create another.
takeaways.zh: 修改后应重新从多种标准检查设计，因为解决一个问题可能产生另一个问题。

exercise.en: Rank three uncertainties by how badly they could hurt the game. Prototype the highest-risk one, record what you learned, and name the next decision before adding features.
exercise.zh: 按可能造成的影响为三个不确定因素排序。针对风险最高的一项制作原型，记录所得结论，并在增加功能前明确下一步决策。

title.en: The Game Is Made for a Player

summary.en: Understanding an audience requires moving beyond the designer’s own preferences. The chapter considers demographic groupings but also looks at psychographics: the kinds of pleasure and activity different players seek.
summary.zh: 理解受众需要超越设计师自己的偏好。本章考察人口统计分组，也关注心理特征，即不同玩家所追求的愉悦与活动。

takeaways.en: Treat categories as prompts for investigation, not as guarantees about an individual player.
takeaways.zh: 将分类作为调查线索，而不是对某个玩家的必然判断。

takeaways.en: Ask what someone enjoys doing and feeling, rather than assuming that outward characteristics explain their preferences.
takeaways.zh: 询问一个人喜欢做什么、获得什么感受，不要假定外在特征就能解释其偏好。

exercise.en: Interview two potential players with different habits. Identify one shared pleasure and one conflicting preference, then decide which the current prototype will serve.
exercise.zh: 访谈两位习惯不同的潜在玩家。找出一种共同愉悦与一项冲突偏好，再决定当前原型要服务哪一种需求。

title.en: The Experience Is in the Player’s Mind

summary.en: Players construct simplified mental models, direct attention selectively, empathize, and fill gaps with imagination. Good design works with those processes instead of assuming that every detail on screen is noticed or understood.
summary.zh: 玩家会建立简化的心智模型、选择性地分配注意力、产生共情，并用想象填补空白。好的设计顺应这些过程，而不是假定屏幕上的每个细节都会被注意或理解。

takeaways.en: Clear goals and a suitable relationship between challenge and skill help sustain focused play.
takeaways.zh: 清晰的目标，以及挑战与技能之间恰当的关系，有助于维持专注的游玩。

takeaways.en: Provide the cues players need to form a useful model; imagination can supply details that need not be explicitly rendered.
takeaways.zh: 提供建立有效模型所需的线索；一些不必明确呈现的细节可以由想象补足。

exercise.en: Watch a new player attempt one task without explanation. Ask them what they think the system is doing, then change one cue that would repair their mistaken model.
exercise.zh: 不作解释，观察一名新玩家尝试完成任务。询问他们认为系统如何运作，再修改一个能纠正错误模型的提示。

title.en: The Player’s Mind Is Driven by the Player’s Motivation
title.zh: 玩家的心智由动机驱动

summary.en: The chapter compares ways of understanding motivation: needs, intrinsic and extrinsic rewards, pleasure seeking, pain avoidance, novelty, and judgment. These perspectives help explain why the same activity can feel inviting or compulsory.
summary.zh: 本章比较了理解动机的多种视角：需求、内外在奖励、寻求愉悦、回避痛苦、新奇感与评判。它们帮助解释为什么同一活动可能令人向往，也可能像一项义务。

takeaways.en: Competence, autonomy, and relatedness offer useful questions about the experience beyond the reward schedule.
takeaways.zh: 胜任、自主与联结，让我们能在奖励安排之外进一步追问体验质量。

takeaways.en: More rewards do not automatically strengthen the motivation that made the activity appealing in the first place.
takeaways.zh: 更多奖励并不自动强化最初让活动具有吸引力的动机。

exercise.en: For one daily or repeated activity, list why a player wants to do it and why they might feel forced to do it. Change one obligation into a choice and compare responses.
exercise.zh: 针对一项日常或重复活动，列出玩家想做它的原因，以及可能觉得被迫去做的原因。将一项义务改为选择，再比较反应。

title.en: Some Elements Are Game Mechanics

summary.en: The chapter gives a vocabulary for describing what a game does: space, time, objects, actions, rules, skill, and chance. It connects formal structure to strategic possibilities and to players’ uncertain judgments about outcomes.
summary.zh: 本章用空间、时间、对象、行动、规则、技能与运气来描述游戏如何运作，并将形式结构与策略可能性、玩家对不确定结果的判断联系起来。

takeaways.en: Track which information changes, who knows it, and which actions can alter it; these choices shape strategy.
takeaways.zh: 追踪哪些信息会变化、谁知道这些信息，以及什么行动能改变它们；这些选择会塑造策略。

takeaways.en: Separate actual probabilities and expected values from what players perceive; both affect the experience.
takeaways.zh: 区分真实概率、期望值与玩家感知；它们都会影响体验。

exercise.en: Model a small encounter as states and actions. For one risky action, calculate its expected payoff and ask a player to estimate the odds before revealing the numbers.
exercise.zh: 将一个小型遭遇建模为状态与行动。计算其中一项风险行动的期望收益，并在公布数值前请玩家估计胜算。

title.en: Game Mechanics Must Be in Balance

summary.en: Balance involves several relationships, not just making every option numerically equal. The chapter connects fairness, challenge, meaningful choice, rewards, punishment, complexity, and economic decisions to the experience you want players to have.
summary.zh: 平衡涉及多种关系，并不只是让所有选项在数值上相等。本章把公平、挑战、有意义的选择、奖励、惩罚、复杂性与经济决策，联系到设计师期望的玩家体验。

takeaways.en: Different player powers can still be fair; equal starting conditions and equal experiences are different goals.
takeaways.zh: 玩家拥有不同能力也可以公平；起点相等与体验相等是不同目标。

takeaways.en: A safer low-reward option and a riskier high-reward option become interesting only when the trade-off is credible.
takeaways.zh: 低风险低回报与高风险高回报之间的取舍，只有在权衡可信时才有趣。

exercise.en: Choose two competing strategies and test them with a novice and an experienced player. Record when each becomes attractive, then adjust one cost or reward instead of changing everything at once.
exercise.zh: 选择两种竞争策略，请新手与熟练玩家分别测试。记录每种策略何时有吸引力，再只调整一项成本或奖励，避免同时改变所有因素。

title.en: Game Mechanics Support Puzzles

summary.en: Puzzles give players reasons to pause, reason, and discover. The chapter treats clear goals, a visible starting point, progress, and support for getting unstuck as parts of a sustained thinking experience.
summary.zh: 谜题让玩家有理由停下来推理与发现。本章把清晰目标、明确起点、进展感以及脱困支持，视为持续思考体验的组成部分。

takeaways.en: A puzzle can be difficult while still making its goal and the possibility of a solution clear.
takeaways.zh: 谜题可以很难，同时仍让目标和可解性清晰可见。

takeaways.en: Parallel challenges, gradual steps, and hints can preserve interest when one obstacle would otherwise block all progress.
takeaways.zh: 当单个障碍可能阻断全部进展时，并行挑战、渐进步骤与提示可以维持兴趣。

exercise.en: Draw the dependency graph for a puzzle sequence. Identify a single point of failure and add either an independent challenge or a hint that preserves the central discovery.
exercise.zh: 画出一组谜题的依赖关系图。找出一个会阻断全部进展的节点，再增加独立挑战或保留核心发现的提示。

title.en: Players Play Games through an Interface

summary.en: An interface is the complete path between a player’s intentions and the game’s responses. Physical controls, virtual displays, feedback, information channels, and modes all contribute to whether players feel capable and in control.
summary.zh: 界面是连接玩家意图与游戏回应的完整路径。物理操作、虚拟显示、反馈、信息通道与模式，共同决定玩家是否感到胜任且能够掌控。

takeaways.en: Prioritize information before deciding where and how to show it; several messages can compete for the same channel.
takeaways.zh: 先确定信息优先级，再决定在哪里、以何种方式呈现；多条信息可能争夺同一通道。

takeaways.en: Metaphors and modes help only when they support expectations; transitions need recognizable feedback.
takeaways.zh: 隐喻与模式只有在支持预期时才有帮助；模式切换需要易于识别的反馈。

exercise.en: Trace one action from input to game-state change to feedback. Remove an unnecessary step and provide a second, complementary cue for its most important result.
exercise.zh: 追踪一次行动从输入到游戏状态变化、再到反馈的全过程。移除一个不必要的步骤，并为最重要的结果提供第二种互补提示。

title.en: Experiences Can Be Judged by Their Interest Curves

summary.en: An interest curve describes how engagement changes across an experience. The chapter connects memorable moments with pacing, presentation, and the player’s ability to project into what is happening.
summary.zh: 兴趣曲线描述投入程度如何在体验中变化。本章把难忘时刻与节奏、呈现方式，以及玩家对事件的代入联系起来。

takeaways.en: A curve is useful for relative changes in interest, not as a precise universal measurement of fun.
takeaways.zh: 曲线适合比较兴趣的相对变化，并非对乐趣进行精确、普适的测量。

takeaways.en: A compelling overall arc can contain smaller arcs; rest and contrast help powerful moments stand out.
takeaways.zh: 吸引人的整体曲线可以包含较小的曲线；休息与反差帮助有力的时刻脱颖而出。

exercise.en: Sketch your intended interest curve for a ten-minute session. Ask a tester to sketch theirs afterward, compare the largest mismatch, and redesign that moment.
exercise.zh: 画出一段十分钟试玩的预期兴趣曲线。试玩后请测试者画出自己的曲线，比较差异最大的地方，并重新设计那个时刻。

title.en: One Kind of Experience Is the Story

summary.en: Games can deliver an authored sequence or generate stories through play. The chapter examines why unlimited branching does not automatically produce satisfying narrative, and how goals, obstacles, consistency, and emotional change support story.
summary.zh: 游戏既可以呈现预先创作的序列，也可以通过游玩生成故事。本章分析了为何无限分支并不自动带来满意的叙事，以及目标、障碍、一致性与情感变化如何支持故事。

takeaways.en: A branching structure creates production and coherence problems; more choices alone do not solve them.
takeaways.zh: 分支结构会带来制作成本与连贯性问题；单纯增加选择无法解决它们。

takeaways.en: Narrative should work with the game’s other elements and the player’s actions rather than being attached as an independent script.
takeaways.zh: 叙事应与游戏的其他要素和玩家行动协作，而不是作为独立剧本附加上去。

exercise.en: Take one scene and state the player’s goal, obstacle, and meaningful action. Explain how the outcome changes the story, then remove a branch that adds cost without a distinct experience.
exercise.zh: 选择一个场景，明确玩家的目标、障碍与有意义的行动。说明结果如何改变故事，再移除一个只增加成本、却不带来独特体验的分支。

title.en: Story and Game Structures Can Be Artfully Merged with Indirect Control
title.zh: 以间接控制融合故事与游戏

summary.en: The feeling of freedom can coexist with a deliberately shaped experience. The chapter explains how constraints, goals, interfaces, visuals, characters, and music can guide attention and action without requiring constant explicit instructions.
summary.zh: 自由感可以与经过设计的体验共存。本章解释约束、目标、界面、视觉、角色和音乐如何引导注意力与行动，而不必始终依赖明确指令。

takeaways.en: Players’ expectations about what they can do are shaped by the choices and cues the design presents.
takeaways.zh: 设计所呈现的选择与线索，会塑造玩家对自己能做什么的预期。

takeaways.en: Characters can support the intended experience while still behaving consistently with their own world and goals.
takeaways.zh: 角色可以支持预期体验，同时仍与自身所在世界和目标保持一致。

exercise.en: Choose a place where players miss the intended route. Replace a direct instruction with a visual, goal-based, or character cue, then observe whether players still feel they chose freely.
exercise.zh: 选择一处玩家经常错过预期路线的地方。用视觉、目标或角色线索替换直接指令，再观察玩家是否仍觉得是自己自由作出的选择。

title.en: Stories and Games Take Place in Worlds
title.zh: 故事与游戏发生在世界中

summary.en: A fictional world can support more than one story or medium. The chapter examines how persistent fantasies, recognizable qualities, and multiple entry points help people maintain a relationship with a world over time.
summary.zh: 一个虚构世界可以承载不止一个故事或媒介。本章考察持久的幻想、可辨识的特质与多种入口，如何帮助人们长期与这个世界保持联系。

takeaways.en: A world should offer something people want to imagine being or doing, beyond following one plot.
takeaways.zh: 世界应提供人们想象成为某个人、或从事某种活动的可能，而不只是跟随单一情节。

takeaways.en: Different media can open different doors into the same world; each should contribute to a coherent whole.
takeaways.zh: 不同媒介可以打开通往同一世界的不同入口；每个入口都应服务于连贯的整体。

exercise.en: Write three promises your world makes to a visitor. Show how a game and a short story could deliver different parts of those promises without contradicting each other.
exercise.zh: 写出你的世界向访客作出的三个承诺。说明游戏与短篇故事如何各自实现不同部分，同时不相互矛盾。

title.en: Worlds Contain Characters

summary.en: Characters have jobs within the game as well as personalities within the fiction. The chapter connects avatar projection with character functions, traits, relationships, status, and believable change.
summary.zh: 角色既在游戏中承担职能，也在虚构世界中拥有个性。本章将化身代入与角色功能、特质、关系、地位和可信的变化联系起来。

takeaways.en: Define what the game needs a character to do, then make their traits visible in words, actions, and appearance.
takeaways.zh: 先定义游戏需要角色做什么，再让其特质通过言语、行动和外表表现出来。

takeaways.en: Map how characters feel about one another; varied relationships create possibilities that isolated biographies miss.
takeaways.zh: 画出角色彼此的感受；多样的关系能产生孤立人物传记无法呈现的可能。

exercise.en: Choose three characters and write a directed relationship between every pair. Give each character one gameplay function and one action that reveals their defining trait.
exercise.zh: 选择三个角色，为每对角色写下有方向的关系。再给每个角色指定一种玩法职能，以及一个揭示其核心特质的行动。

title.en: Worlds Contain Spaces

summary.en: Game spaces organize activity and feeling, not just geometry. The chapter draws on architecture to connect movement, landmarks, coherent structure, and the player’s experience of a place.
summary.zh: 游戏空间组织的不只是几何形状，还有活动与感受。本章借鉴建筑学，将移动、地标、协调的结构与玩家对场所的体验联系起来。

takeaways.en: Choose spatial organization according to its purpose; virtual spaces need not obey every constraint of real buildings.
takeaways.zh: 依据目的选择空间组织方式；虚拟空间不必遵守真实建筑的全部约束。

takeaways.en: A visually impressive space can still undermine play when scale, navigation, or interacting systems contradict its purpose.
takeaways.zh: 如果尺度、导航或相互作用的系统违背目的，视觉震撼的空间仍可能损害游玩。

exercise.en: Sketch one level as routes and landmarks without decoration. Ask where a player should pause, decide, and orient themselves, then check that the geometry supports those moments.
exercise.zh: 去掉装饰，把一个关卡画成路线与地标。确定玩家应在哪里停顿、决策和辨认方向，再检查几何结构是否支持这些时刻。

title.en: Some Interfaces Create a Feeling of Presence

summary.en: Presence is the feeling of being somewhere, and it is particularly important in VR and AR. The chapter treats it as fragile: bodily expectations, interaction, sound, identity, and comfort can strengthen or interrupt it.
summary.zh: 临场感是身处某地的感觉，在 VR 与 AR 中尤其重要。本章强调它的脆弱性：身体预期、交互、声音、身份认同与舒适度都可能加强或打断它。

takeaways.en: Consistent body tracking, hand interaction, and sound help the simulated world agree with what the player expects.
takeaways.zh: 一致的身体追踪、手部交互与声音，有助于模拟世界符合玩家预期。

takeaways.en: Physical mockups can expose spatial and interaction problems before a detailed virtual implementation exists.
takeaways.zh: 在精细的虚拟实现出现之前，实体模型就能暴露空间与交互问题。

exercise.en: Mock up one embodied interaction with cardboard and ordinary objects. Observe reach, orientation, and expected feedback, then record what the virtual version must preserve.
exercise.zh: 用纸板和日常物品模拟一次身体交互。观察伸手范围、朝向与预期反馈，再记录虚拟版本必须保留什么。

title.en: The Look and Feel of a World Is Defined by Its Aesthetics
title.zh: 美感定义世界的外观与感受

summary.en: Aesthetics contributes to the complete experience and can guide design from the beginning. The chapter emphasizes learning to see, using appropriately rough concept work, and treating audio as a powerful design material.
summary.zh: 美感参与构成完整体验，并能从一开始就引导设计。本章强调学会观察、采用精度恰当的概念作品，并把音频视为有力的设计材料。

takeaways.en: Concept art can reveal a shared direction or expose a mismatch before production makes changes expensive.
takeaways.zh: 概念艺术可以在制作成本升高之前，揭示共同方向或暴露理解偏差。

takeaways.en: Sound affects atmosphere and the perceived response to action; it should not be postponed as a finishing touch.
takeaways.zh: 声音影响氛围及玩家对行动回应的感知，不应只作为最后的装饰。

exercise.en: Make a rough visual sketch and a short sound palette for the same scene. Ask which feeling each suggests, and revise them until they support the same intention.
exercise.zh: 为同一场景制作粗略视觉草图与一组简短声音。询问它们各自让人产生什么感受，再修改到二者支持同一意图。

title.en: Some Games Are Played with Other Players
title.zh: 有些游戏与其他玩家一起玩

summary.en: Other people add experiences a single-player system cannot fully supply. The chapter considers competition, cooperation, social connection, spectatorship, and the trust needed for multiplayer play to feel worthwhile.
summary.zh: 其他人能带来单人系统无法完全提供的体验。本章讨论竞争、合作、社交联结、观赏性，以及让多人游玩值得投入的信任。

takeaways.en: Design for what players get from one another instead of treating multiplayer as merely adding more participants.
takeaways.zh: 围绕玩家能从彼此获得什么来设计，不要把多人模式仅仅当作增加参与人数。

takeaways.en: Spectators need something understandable and interesting to watch, while participants need confidence that the contest is trustworthy.
takeaways.zh: 观众需要易于理解且有趣的内容，参与者则需要相信较量值得信任。

exercise.en: Observe one match from a spectator’s position. List what is hard to understand, then inspect one rule or exploit that could make participants doubt the fairness of the outcome.
exercise.zh: 从观众位置观察一场对局，列出难以理解的部分，再检查一项可能让参与者怀疑结果公平性的规则或漏洞。

title.en: Other Players Sometimes Form Communities

summary.en: A community gives players reasons to return that extend beyond the game's formal goals. Its design involves helping people meet, express themselves, develop relationships, and find a continuing place in the group.
summary.zh: 社群让玩家获得超越游戏正式目标的回归理由。设计社群，需要帮助人们相遇、表达自我、建立关系，并持续找到自己在群体中的位置。

takeaways.en: Consider the different needs of newcomers, regular participants, and experienced members.
takeaways.zh: 考虑新成员、常驻成员与资深成员各自不同的需要。

takeaways.en: Shared activities and opportunities to contribute can support relationships; conflict also needs deliberate handling.
takeaways.zh: 共同活动与贡献机会有助于建立关系；冲突同样需要有意识地处理。

exercise.en: Sketch a newcomer's first three visits to your community. Identify one welcoming interaction and one useful contribution they can make without prior expertise.
exercise.zh: 画出新成员前三次进入社群的经历，设计一次友好的互动，以及一项无需既有经验也能做出的有用贡献。

title.en: The Designer Usually Works with a Team
title.zh: 设计师通常与团队合作

summary.en: Game design becomes a shared activity when specialists bring different skills and perspectives to a project. Schell emphasizes commitment to the game and its audience, supported by communication and trust, as foundations for productive collaboration.
summary.zh: 当不同专业的人将各自技能与视角带入项目时，游戏设计就成为共同活动。Schell 强调，对游戏及其受众的投入，以及沟通与信任，是有效协作的基础。

takeaways.en: Shared enthusiasm is more useful when teammates also understand the experience they are trying to create.
takeaways.zh: 团队的共同热情需要建立在对目标体验的理解之上。

takeaways.en: Make room for design contributions across disciplines and clarify how decisions are reached.
takeaways.zh: 让不同专业的人都有机会参与设计，并明确决策如何形成。

exercise.en: Ask each teammate to describe the intended player experience in one sentence. Compare the answers and agree on a concrete example that resolves the largest difference.
exercise.zh: 请每位成员用一句话描述目标玩家体验，比较答案，再用一个具体例子化解最大的分歧。

title.en: The Team Sometimes Communicates through Documents
title.zh: 团队有时通过文档沟通

summary.en: Design documents support memory and communication as a project changes. A useful document answers the needs of its readers; a single exhaustive design document is unlikely to serve every discipline and stage equally well.
summary.zh: 项目不断变化，设计文档帮助团队记忆与沟通。有用的文档应回应读者的需要；一份包罗万象的设计文档，很难同时满足所有专业和阶段。

takeaways.en: Choose the document's detail and format according to the people who will use it.
takeaways.zh: 根据实际使用者选择文档的细节程度与形式。

takeaways.en: Keep decisions, open questions, and changes understandable rather than treating documentation as a one-time deliverable.
takeaways.zh: 让决策、待解问题与变更保持清晰，不要把文档视为一次性交付物。

exercise.en: Choose a confusing feature and write a one-page note for its implementer: intended experience, current decision, example, and unresolved question. Ask whether it enables the next action.
exercise.zh: 选择一个容易误解的功能，为实现者写一页说明：目标体验、当前决策、示例与待解问题。请对方判断它是否足以支持下一步行动。

title.en: Good Games Are Created through Playtesting
title.zh: 好游戏通过游戏测试创造

summary.en: Playtesting investigates what players actually experience and gives iteration new evidence. It serves a different purpose from finding software defects, checking interface usability, or asking a focus group what it thinks of a concept, even when these activities overlap.
summary.zh: 游戏测试研究玩家实际经历了什么，为迭代提供新证据。它与查找软件缺陷、检查界面可用性或询问焦点小组对概念的看法，目的有所不同，尽管这些活动可能重叠。

takeaways.en: Decide why, who, when, where, what, and how before a test so the session can answer a useful question.
takeaways.zh: 测试前明确为什么测、谁来测、何时何地测、测什么及如何测，让测试能够回答有价值的问题。

takeaways.en: Observe behavior as well as listening to comments; the designer's presence and explanations can influence the result.
takeaways.zh: 既听取评论，也观察行为；设计师的在场与解释可能影响结果。

exercise.en: Write one experience question and two observable signals for your next playtest. Plan a neutral follow-up question and one design decision that each possible result would inform.
exercise.zh: 为下一次游戏测试写下一个体验问题与两个可观察信号，准备一个中立的追问，并说明不同结果将如何影响设计决策。

title.en: The Team Builds a Game with Technology
title.zh: 团队利用技术构建游戏

summary.en: Technology both enables and constrains design. The chapter distinguishes technology that a game fundamentally depends on from technology that embellishes it, and examines why excitement about new platforms should be considered alongside practical development needs.
summary.zh: 技术既赋予设计能力，也限制设计。本章区分游戏根本依赖的技术与用于增色的技术，并讨论为何对新平台的热情必须结合实际开发需要来判断。

takeaways.en: Identify which technical assumptions are essential to the intended experience and test them early.
takeaways.zh: 找出目标体验不可缺少的技术假设，并尽早验证。

takeaways.en: Treat the chapter's platform examples and predictions as historical context, not current specifications or market facts.
takeaways.zh: 把本章的平台案例与预测视为历史语境，不作为当前规格或市场事实。

exercise.en: List three technologies your concept uses. For each, describe what experience would be lost without it and design a small test for the most uncertain dependency.
exercise.zh: 列出概念使用的三项技术，分别说明缺少它会失去什么体验，并针对最不确定的一项依赖设计小型验证。

title.en: Your Game Will Probably Have a Client

summary.en: A client may express a desired solution without fully articulating the need behind it. Understanding that need, communicating clearly, and building trust help a designer propose work that serves the client while protecting the intended player experience.
summary.zh: 客户可能提出想要的方案，却未充分说明背后的需要。理解这种需要、清晰沟通并建立信任，有助于设计师提出既服务客户、又照顾目标玩家体验的方案。

takeaways.en: Distinguish a requested feature from the problem the client hopes it will solve.
takeaways.zh: 区分客户要求的功能与他们希望解决的问题。

takeaways.en: Questions and demonstrations can reveal differences between stated expectations and actual needs.
takeaways.zh: 提问与演示有助于揭示表面期待与实际需要之间的差异。

exercise.en: Take a hypothetical client request such as 'add a leaderboard.' Write three possible underlying needs, then propose a question and a small demonstration to distinguish them.
exercise.zh: 以“加入排行榜”等假设客户需求为例，写出三个可能的深层需要，再提出一个问题与一次小型演示来区分它们。

title.en: The Designer Gives the Client a Pitch
title.zh: 设计师向客户推介方案

summary.en: A pitch is an opportunity to show why a game is valuable to a particular audience and partner. Its effectiveness depends on preparation, a clear presentation of the experience, and an understanding of the listener's interests as well as the designer's own goals.
summary.zh: 方案推介旨在说明游戏为何对特定受众与合作方有价值。有效推介需要充分准备、清楚呈现体验，并理解听众的利益及设计师自己的目标。

takeaways.en: Shape the pitch around the listener and the opportunity instead of reciting every feature.
takeaways.zh: 围绕听众与合作机会组织推介，而不是逐项罗列所有功能。

takeaways.en: Rehearse the presentation and use demonstrations or supporting materials that make the proposed experience tangible.
takeaways.zh: 演练表达，并通过演示或辅助材料让目标体验变得具体。

exercise.en: Prepare a two-minute pitch for one named type of partner. Include the player, the core experience, evidence that it can work, and the specific next step you want.
exercise.zh: 为一种明确的合作方准备两分钟推介，包含目标玩家、核心体验、可行性证据，以及希望对方采取的具体下一步。

title.en: The Designer and Client Want the Game to Make a Profit
title.zh: 设计师与客户希望游戏盈利

summary.en: The business surrounding a game affects what can be made and sustained. Designers benefit from understanding costs, revenue models, competition, and the reasons an audience might pay, so commercial assumptions can be discussed together with the experience.
summary.zh: 游戏所处的商业环境影响哪些作品能够制作并持续运营。理解成本、收入模式、竞争与受众付费理由，有助于设计师将商业假设与体验一起讨论。

takeaways.en: A revenue model changes incentives and may shape the player's relationship with the game.
takeaways.zh: 收入模式会改变激励，并可能影响玩家与游戏的关系。

takeaways.en: Make business assumptions explicit; the book's examples are starting points for investigation rather than present-day financial estimates.
takeaways.zh: 明确写出商业假设；书中案例是调查的起点，不是当下的财务估算。

exercise.en: Write a simple model of who pays, what they receive, and the main costs. Identify the least-supported assumption and how you could investigate it before increasing scope.
exercise.zh: 写出一个简单模型：谁付费、获得什么、主要成本是什么。找出证据最不足的假设，并说明扩大规模前如何调查它。

title.en: Games Transform Their Players

summary.en: Games can be designed to produce changes beyond the play session, including learning and other forms of personal development. Transformational goals need to be specific and connected to the game's activities, its audience, and evidence of effects outside the game.
summary.zh: 游戏可以被设计为在游玩结束后仍带来改变，包括学习与其他个人发展。转化目标需要具体，并与游戏活动、受众以及游戏之外的效果证据相联系。

takeaways.en: Work with relevant experts to connect the intended transformation to what players actually practice.
takeaways.zh: 与相关专家合作，让目标改变与玩家实际练习的行为相对应。

takeaways.en: Enjoyment or in-game success alone does not demonstrate that a desired real-world change has occurred.
takeaways.zh: 仅凭愉悦感或游戏内成功，不能证明期望的现实改变已经发生。

exercise.en: Choose one modest learning goal. Map it to a player action, then define an observation outside the game that would provide evidence of transfer.
exercise.zh: 选择一个适度的学习目标，将其对应到玩家动作，再定义一项游戏外的观察，用于判断学习是否发生迁移。

title.en: Designers Have Certain Responsibilities

summary.en: Design decisions can affect people beyond the immediate entertainment experience. Schell asks designers to consider both beneficial and harmful consequences and to take responsibility for the kinds of interactions and habits their games encourage.
summary.zh: 设计决策对人的影响可能超越当下的娱乐体验。Schell 要求设计师同时思考有益与有害的后果，并对游戏所鼓励的互动方式与习惯承担责任。

takeaways.en: Consider how systems and social interactions can produce harm, not only whether individual content is objectionable.
takeaways.zh: 不仅检查单项内容是否不当，也要考虑系统与社交互动如何产生伤害。

takeaways.en: Connect ethical intentions to concrete design choices and evidence from players.
takeaways.zh: 将伦理意图落实到具体设计选择，并结合玩家证据检视。

exercise.en: Review one reward or social system. Describe who benefits, who might be disadvantaged, and one change that reduces the risk while preserving the intended experience.
exercise.zh: 检查一个奖励或社交系统，说明谁受益、谁可能受到不利影响，并提出一项降低风险且保留目标体验的改动。

title.en: Each Designer Has a Purpose

summary.en: The closing numbered chapter turns from project techniques to the designer's own reasons for making games. It asks how limited time, personal purpose, and the effects one hopes to have should influence the work one chooses to pursue.
summary.zh: 最后一个编号章节从项目方法转向设计师制作游戏的自身动机。它追问有限的时间、个人目的与期望带来的影响，应如何改变我们对工作的选择。

takeaways.en: Use awareness of limited time to examine whether today's work serves what matters to you.
takeaways.zh: 借助对时间有限的认识，检视今天的工作是否服务于真正重要的事。

takeaways.en: The book ends its lens sequence with ∞, Your Secret Purpose; the archived web deck identifies the same lens as 113.
takeaways.zh: 原书以 ∞“你的隐秘目的”结束透镜序列；本仓库备份的网络卡牌将同一透镜标为 113。

exercise.en: Write a private sentence about why you want to make games. Choose one small change to your next project that would make its development or effects more consistent with that purpose.
exercise.zh: 私下写一句话，说明你为何想制作游戏。为下一个项目选择一项小改变，让开发过程或作品影响更符合这个目的。
